target.title: fix(secrets): keep startup alive when TTS SecretRefs are missing
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 6, 2026, 10:00 PM (US Eastern Time) / 02:00 UTC.
Last body edit: July 15, 2026, 3:56 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:56 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 15, 2026, 3:47 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:47 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #101204

## What Problem This Solves

A configured but temporarily missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef currently aborts Gateway startup and takes unrelated chat, auth, tools, channels, and plugins offline even though only speech synthesis needs that credential. This PR keeps the first activating startup available while preserving strict failure for every non-activating, reload, restart-check, config-write, malformed-ref, policy, provider, contract, mismatch, and invalid-value path.

## Summary

A missing built-in TTS provider API-key SecretRef no longer aborts an otherwise healthy Gateway during the first activating startup. The affected TTS provider remains unconfigured, startup emits a structured warning, and unrelated chat, auth, tools, channels, and plugins continue to start.

The exception is deliberately narrow. It requires all of the following:

- the lifecycle reason is `startup`;
- the operation will activate the prepared snapshot (`activate === true`);
- no active secrets runtime snapshot exists;
- the assignment is a built-in TTS provider API key explicitly marked optional; and
- resolution failed with the matching missing-value error for that exact ref.

Non-activating startup preparation, restart checks, reloads, config-write preflight, malformed refs, policy/security failures, provider failures, contract failures, mismatched errors, and invalid resolved value shapes remain fail-closed.

## Breaking changes

There is no config-shape, RPC, persistence, package, or dependency change. Failure timing changes for one credential class: a missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef is reported as a startup warning and fails locally when that TTS provider is used, rather than aborting the entire first activating Gateway startup.

## Why / user impact

Built-in TTS is an optional capability, but SecretRef activation previously treated its API keys as credentials required by the whole Gateway. Operators may now keep an optional ElevenLabs or other built-in TTS SecretRef configured while its value is temporarily absent. The provider remains unavailable until the ref resolves, while unrelated Gateway capabilities stay online.

The stricter sibling paths are unchanged: reload, restart-check, non-activating startup preparation, and config-write preflight reject the unresolved ref and preserve the last-known-good runtime/config.

## Implementation

- `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` owns the lifecycle gate. Optional missing-value degradation is enabled only for `reason === "startup"`, `activate === true`, and an absent active runtime snapshot.
- The lifecycle gate is layered onto the current mainline `resolveGatewayStartupSecretProjection` contract. `sourceConfig` remains the recoverable full source, while an `assignmentConfig` may suppress unsafe channel assignments during crash-loop recovery; this PR does not collapse those responsibilities back into one pruned config.
- `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.ts` marks only built-in TTS provider API-key assignments as optional at startup.
- `src/secrets/resolve-errors.ts` owns typed provider/ref errors and the exact missing-value classifier; `src/secrets/resolve.ts` assigns those codes at env/file/exec and provider-contract boundaries.
- `src/secrets/runtime-optional-assignments.ts` owns required/optional partitioning, independent optional resolution, warning emission, and redaction registration.
- `src/secrets/runtime-prepare.runtime.ts` exports that helper through the existing lazy startup facade, so the Gateway hot path does not statically load the full resolver.
- `src/secrets/runtime.ts` delegates assignment resolution once and remains focused on snapshot preparation/activation.
- `src/secrets/runtime-shared.ts` carries optional-assignment metadata while retaining existing resolved-value shape validation.

## Code-path analysis

- Runtime entry: `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` prepares secrets before Gateway startup activation.
- Lifecycle owner: `createRuntimeSecretsActivator` decides whether preparation is activating and whether a prior runtime snapshot exists.
- Mainline projection boundary: `src/gateway/server-startup-secret-surfaces.ts` separates recoverable source config from the assignment projection used during crash-loop recovery.
- Snapshot owner: `src/secrets/runtime.ts` prepares and activates the runtime snapshot.
- Optional-assignment owner: `src/secrets/runtime-optional-assignments.ts` resolves optional refs independently without weakening the required batch.
- Collector/caller: `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors.ts` routes core/channel/plugin surfaces; `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.ts` collects top-level, agent, and channel voice TTS API keys.
- Resolver/callee: `src/secrets/resolve.ts` resolves env/file/exec refs; `src/secrets/resolve-errors.ts` distinguishes absence from policy, validation, provider, and contract failures.
- Sibling invariant: Gateway auth, model/provider, plugin, channel-token, auth-store, and all other required assignments remain fail-closed.
- Localized runtime failure: `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts` returns the normal provider-not-configured `UNAVAILABLE` path when the degraded provider is selected.
- Adjacent coverage: `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime-discord-surface.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.test.ts`.

## Mainline comparison

Rebased onto `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@4f71a2855e538185d16e7b04d3acc7f2f02a3944` (commit time 2026-07-15T07:43:03Z; fetched 2026-07-15T07:47Z).

Recent same-area mainline work was incorporated rather than overwritten:

- `701d02f241` made the Gateway startup secret-assignment projection explicit.
- `1eec68a6a0` preserved safe-mode secret recovery when suppressed channel secrets are unavailable.
- `3616fba951` made hot reload transactional.

The final rebase increment through `4f71a2855e` changed unrelated auto-reply tests, status formatting, signed-merge handling, Codex restricted-turn shell behavior, and Telegram archive fixtures. During the final exact-head proof, official `main` advanced through `1fe3a5f557` with plugin compatibility, terminal quoting, Codex adapter, and Testbox path changes; the GitHub compare contains no changes under this PR's startup lifecycle gate, `src/secrets/`, or TTS docs/tests.

## Branch / base provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@4f71a2855e538185d16e7b04d3acc7f2f02a3944`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/optional-tts-secret-startup@9a4986f4c3bafd96c69568794e522060c3e0608c`
- Evidence branch: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:proof/issue-101204-live@5c712d5c05475d5984ce73b36309202d2c367896`
- The evidence commit's direct parent is the exact PR head.
- The fork default branch remains mirror-only and was not modified by this work.
- `Allow edits by maintainers` remains enabled.

## Dependency / contract verification

No dependency, lockfile, package, protocol, persisted schema, database, sidecar, or config-schema changes are included. The resolver error code is internal runtime classification used to preserve the existing fail-closed contract except for the explicitly optional, missing-value-only, first-activation TTS case.

No migration or upgrade compatibility step is required. Tests that serialize fixture configs or exercise the runtime cache do not alter a persisted data model.

## Labels considered

Observed automated labels include `gateway`, `docs`, compatibility risk, and security-boundary risk. No contributor-side label mutation was performed. The compatibility and security labels remain appropriate because the PR deliberately changes startup behavior for one credential class inside the shared secrets runtime.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` — passed on the current head.
- [Exact-head focused tests and live Gateway/RPC proof](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29398667816) — passed on evidence head `5c712d5c05475d5984ce73b36309202d2c367896`, whose direct parent is code head `9a4986f4c3bafd96c69568794e522060c3e0608c`. The run passed 90 focused tests, started a real Gateway with the missing TTS ref, observed the structured warning, and verified localized `tts.speak` failure while the Gateway stayed available.
- [Full upstream CI on the byte-equivalent rebased patch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29397794848) — passed: 45 jobs successful and 11 skipped on `8e7cfaf489ec194bdb160bfcb881d8a55bb267d6`. The final rebase only advanced across unrelated mainline commits; stable patch-id for the complete PR diff remained `eec8e924514251d650ca5a89d501be1517bcd1b7`.
- Exact-current-head PR gates passed for CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep PR diff, Workflow Sanity, Security Sensitive Guard, Dependency Guard, and the upstream Real behavior proof dispatcher. The current full CI and CodeQL runs remain linked in the PR check rollup.

## Evidence source map

[Evidence workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29398667816)

- Purpose: focused resolver/runtime/TTS collector/Discord voice/Gateway startup/TTS handler regression suite plus live Gateway/RPC behavior.
- Conclusion: success.
- Evidence commit: `5c712d5c05475d5984ce73b36309202d2c367896`.
- Exact code parent: `9a4986f4c3bafd96c69568794e522060c3e0608c`.
- Environment: GitHub-hosted Linux runner, Node.js 24.
- Artifact: focused-test and live-proof text logs uploaded by the run.
- PR-only workflow, harness, and logs remain on the dedicated evidence branch and are absent from the code diff.

## Sanitized logs

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       33 passed (33)
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       57 passed (57)
Gateway started with missing optional ELEVENLABS_API_KEY SecretRef.
[SECRETS_REF_UNAVAILABLE_OPTIONAL] messages.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey ... Environment variable "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY" is missing or empty.
TTS conversion failed: elevenlabs: not configured
PASS: missing optional TTS SecretRef degraded startup and localized TTS failure.
```

The proof uses placeholder credential identifiers and redacts generated tokens, temporary paths, and dynamic local addresses.

## Media evidence

This change has no UI or visual state. The relevant behavior is a deterministic startup lifecycle plus RPC path, so the complete Actions execution and uploaded logs provide stronger evidence than a screenshot or video. No timing-dependent user interaction is involved.

## Risk

- Compatibility: operators who relied on whole-Gateway fail-fast for an optional TTS key will now discover that missing value when TTS is used.
- Security boundary: the exception lives in shared secrets startup code, so it is gated by lifecycle state, assignment metadata, exact ref matching, and the typed missing-value classifier.
- Lifecycle regression: non-activating startup preparation, restart-check, reload, active-snapshot startup preparation, and config-write preflight are explicitly covered as strict paths.
- Performance: optional refs are resolved independently; work is bounded by configured built-in TTS provider keys and avoids one missing optional provider masking another valid provider.
- Required credentials, policy denials, invalid refs, provider/contract errors, mismatched refs, and invalid resolved shapes remain fatal and are covered by regression tests.

## Rollback

Revert the two PR commits. No config, database, cache, serialized state, or data migration rollback is required. Existing SecretRefs remain valid; rollback restores universal startup fail-fast behavior for missing built-in TTS provider keys.

## Docs updated

- `docs/gateway/secrets.md`
- `docs/reference/secretref-credential-surface.md`
- `docs/tools/tts.md`

The docs describe the missing-value-only first-activation exception and the normal localized provider-not-configured error.

## Related issue / PR

- Canonical issue: #101204
- Duplicate report: #101205
- Adjacent persona-level SecretRef work: #89607 and #89636 (collection/injection scope, not missing-value startup policy)

## Not tested / limitations

- The live Gateway proof covers a missing env-backed ElevenLabs key.
- Missing file values are covered by optional-runtime tests; missing exec-provider ids are covered by resolver classification tests rather than separate live Gateway runs.
- No real provider API call is attempted because the behavior under test is the absent-credential boundary.
- This PR does not add a persistent `degraded` / `configured_unavailable` state or a new status/doctor/audit projection. It provides the structured startup warning and localized runtime failure; broader observability remains a separate product-scope decision.
- Maintainer product acceptance is still required for the scoped fail-open startup policy.

## Review context addressed

The P1 lifecycle finding is resolved by requiring `activationParams.activate === true` in addition to `reason === "startup"` and no active snapshot. A dedicated regression now proves that non-activating startup preparation with no active snapshot remains fail-closed. Restart-check, reload, active-snapshot preparation, and config-write preflight strictness remain covered.

The previous proof-provenance blocker is also resolved: the final evidence commit's direct parent is the exact PR code head, and the linked run exercises both the focused suite and the live Gateway/RPC path on that parent.
